# Independent audit: equal and near-equal endpoint areas with an arbitrary planar middle fiber

Audited in full:

- `candidate f968b5a47e83bb95`;
- `candidate 59cc2a7b6dcd2dbc`.

**PASS.** The source verifier `supporting computation verify_planar_equal_endpoints_arbitrary_middle_two_sided.py` was read and independently rerun: **3,238 exact checks pass**, including actual rational polygons, oblique halfspaces, Minkowski centroids, unequal original denominators, and all displayed constants. This is a proved three-fiber planar regime, not a complete resolution of OC.

## 1. Bodies, fibers, and source points

The lifted convex hull of A at -1, K at 0, and B at 1 is a compact full-dimensional body. Its endpoint fibers are exactly A and B. At level zero, the endpoint weights in any convex combination agree, so the resulting point is a convex combination of a point of K and a point of (A+B)/2. Compatibility therefore makes its zero fiber exactly K. Its integer bases are exactly -1,0,1. In the exact-midpoint source the same argument gives precisely A,M,B.

The centroid g_M is an actual interior point of M and hence of K; g_K is also an actual point of K. These are deterministic sources. The proof does not identify g_M with (g_A+g_B)/2. Ordinary area on the three disjoint planar fibers is exactly the mixed measure used in every denominator.

## 2. Both paired-tail estimates

The residual-BM inequality is the one independently audited in `historical context (not an accepted premise)`. Its proof is repeated correctly: if U+V<a, both residual bodies have positive volume, their midpoint lies in the opposite centroid halfspace of M, and its area is at most 5m/9. The square-root lower estimate follows exactly from (a-U)(a-V)-a(a-U-V)=UV>=0. The rearranged square is nonnegative before squaring because m>=a. The case U+V>=a is immediate, and every boundary line is area-null.

The support-distance estimate is proved without a hidden theorem: after projection normalization to [0,1], the homothet about a lower support point gives CDF(s)>=s^d. Integrating survival gives centroid projection at most d/(d+1). In the plane this yields the summed upper-support cap-height constraint in (6).

For the width bound, a cap contains the homothetic body centered at its upper support point with the appropriate clamped relative height. If one cap is full, its area a already dominates the desired lower bound. Otherwise the positive relative heights lie in [0,1], and replacing a negative height by zero only increases the width-weighted sum. Cauchy--Schwarz gives (7). No supporting, empty, or saturated status is lost. The all-dimensional supplementary Hölder form in the exact-midpoint note is valid for the same reason; it is not used to assert an all-dimensional OC result.

## 3. Section addition and the width-volume relation

After making u a unit normal, use one common affine parameter in the two projection intervals. At the summed projection value, the actual Minkowski section contains the sum of the corresponding two intervals; their one-dimensional lengths add exactly. Integrating with the summed projection Jacobian gives

    4m >= (w_A+w_B)(a/w_A+a/w_B).

This proves R+1/R<=4r-2 for every normal direction. Rescaling u changes the widths and the coarea factor compatibly, so there is no omitted norm factor. Substitution into the Cauchy estimate gives W(r)=2r/[9(2r-1)]. This uses actual common bodies throughout.

The older exact-midpoint note's supplementary segment-extrusion proof is also correct: projection is perpendicular to the actual width-realizing segment, and the line-section bound tracks its obliqueness. It is not confused with projection perpendicular to u.

## 4. All halfspaces and the raw constant

A containing halfspace can be moved inward until its boundary contains the source. With nonzero continuous normal, its endpoint cuts are precisely the oppositely shifted pair in the estimates above. The middle K cap contains the cap of M at g_M, so contributes at least 4m/9. The proof uses 4m/9, not the generally unjustified 4k/9 at g_M.

For 1<=r<=33/20, the residual-based raw expression 4sqrt(5r)/3-16r/9 is concave. Its two endpoint values exceed 308/345: the first exceeds 1, and the second comparison reduces to 33*23^2-132^2=33>0. For r>=33/20, the width-based raw expression is increasing, with derivative 4/9-2/[9(2r-1)^2]>0. Its value at the split is exactly 308/345. Thus every nonvertical through-source cap has at least (308/345)a mass for every r>=1.

A purely integer through-source cap contains all of K and at least one full endpoint, with mass at least k+a>=2a. The boundary middle fiber is counted in full. This closes all ambient halfspaces, including oblique ones and the positive-boundary-mass case.

## 5. Deterministic source switch and original denominators

The ordinary centroid g_K independently guarantees raw mass 4k/9. The better of the two certified raw bounds therefore yields

    max{4k/9,308a/345}/(k+2a).

The first normalized branch increases in k/a and the second decreases. They meet at k/a=231/115, giving 308/1383, whose difference from 2/9 is exactly 2/4149>0. The explicit source-selection rule in the source chooses g_M below this crossing and g_K above it. If k<=2a, the g_M bound alone gives 77/345.

For b>=a, the actual homothetic area-a subset B' stays inside B, and (A+B')/2 stays inside K. Its raw bound transfers monotonically to the original source at the same point. The denominator remains a+b+k, not that of the smaller subsystem. The same switch therefore gives 308/[3(346+115b/a)], and elementary rearrangement proves the exact sufficient ratio bound b/a<=116/115. An arbitrary fixed actual contraction point is enough; taking g_B, for example, makes the construction explicitly deterministic. Reversing the integer coordinate swaps the endpoints without changing any measure or halfspace guarantee.

## 6. The separately stated exact-midpoint margin

When K=M, the simpler paired lower bound max{1/9,F(r)} gives the normalized expression in the exact-midpoint note. F decreases on [1,infinity), and its crossing with 1/9 is r_*=(17+12sqrt(2))/20. On the left branch the normalized derivative has sign 6sqrt(5)(2-r)/sqrt(r)-32<0; on the right the normalized function increases. Its minimum is exactly the displayed lower constant

    kappa=4(22+12sqrt(2))/[9(57+12sqrt(2))]>2/9.

This computation and the positivity certificate for kappa-2/9 are correct. It is an explicitly proved lower bound, not an asserted sharp constant. The arbitrary-middle theorem is the broader scoped conclusion; neither theorem invokes the false linear paired-tail compensation.

## 7. Direct unequal-area extension: the ratio 21/20

The newly appended source Section 6 was independently read in full: **PASS**. The expanded verifier was rerun and passes **5,908 exact checks**. This extension keeps both original endpoint bodies; it does not use the smaller subsystem from Section 5.

For P=U+V<a<=b, the residual-root sum is minimized by spending the captured amount P on the smaller-volume body A. Indeed the two endpoint values of the concave allocation function are sqrt(a-P)+sqrt(b) and sqrt(a)+sqrt(b-P), and the first is smaller because sqrt(x)-sqrt(x-P) decreases in x. The actual residual midpoint bound then gives F_beta(r). Before squaring, the root difference is positive in the stated range since 20r>=20>9beta. The width bound W(r) also survives: B's cap homothet has area at least a times its squared relative height, and the actual unequal-area section-addition inequality dominates its equal-a counterpart.

For 1<=beta<=21/20, r_min=(1+sqrt(beta))^2/4<=beta. The chosen split (19beta+14)/20 lies strictly between r_min and 1+beta. The lower-interval residual difference G_beta is concave. Its value at r_min is strictly greater than 19/20 by the displayed rational bounds. At the split, its positive-square comparison is exactly

    -2781beta^2+3858beta-961>0.

The endpoint values 116 and 9539/400 are correct; concavity in beta proves positivity throughout the permitted interval. The width difference at that split is exactly (46-23beta-19beta^2)/[45(19beta+4)]. Its numerator decreases and remains at least 361/400>0. Since the width-based raw expression increases with r, this closes every r in the nonheavy-middle regime.

Thus g_M has raw depth strictly greater than (4/9)(a+b) whenever k<=a+b. Purely integer caps have mass at least k+a>=2a, which also strictly exceeds that raw budget in this ratio window. If k>a+b, g_K alone has normalized depth strictly greater than 2/9. At k=a+b choose g_M, so strictness is retained at the switch. Both choices lie in the original K, and the normalization is the original a+b+k. The result proves the stated three-fiber planar regime up to endpoint area ratio 21/20 and makes no assertion for all endpoint ratios or higher dimensions.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
